title: Cloud Connector (ztw) Go SDK service functions with wrong assertions, nil payloads, or routing defects
aliases: ztw sdk returns empty admin user
ztw legacy client routes to zia

update-admin-user-zero-result.statement: `UpdateAdminUser` in the ZTW package passes the admin user by value to the PUT helper, which builds its response object with `reflect.New` (a pointer), then asserts the response to the value type `AdminUsers`. The assertion fails, its failure is discarded, and the function returns a pointer to a zero-value `AdminUsers` with a nil error, whatever the server returned.

update-admin-user-zero-result.conditions: This is the same defect as the ZIA admin-user update in [[zia.sdk-go.service-defects]]; the ZTW function reaches the same shared helper. The legacy ZTW client's updater also returns a pointer, so both clients behave the same. On the OneAPI client an empty reply returns nil, nil, the assertion fails the same way and the result is still a zero struct; the legacy client errors on an empty reply instead.

admin-user-update-not-called-by-provider.statement: The ZTC provider at v0.2.0 does not call `UpdateAdminUser`, so the zero-value result does not reach Terraform state. The defect is observable only to other SDK callers.
admin-user-update-not-called-by-provider.conditions: Absence claim from a search: `git -C vendor/terraform-provider-ztc grep -n 'UpdateAdminUser' <ref>` returns no match at v0.2.0 or HEAD (any file, tests included). The quoted line is only an example of a provider update call that does use a ZTW update function and checks its result.

public-cloud-change-state-nil-payload.statement: `UpdatePublicCloudChangeState` sends its change-state PUT with a nil payload. The generic PUT helper (and the legacy ZTW client's) rejects a nil payload with an error before building any request, so the function returns an error on every call and can never change the state.

ztw-services-use-generic-legacy-path.statement: Several ZTW services call the generic `Read`, `Create`, `UpdateWithPut`, and `Delete` on the client, which are the ZIA request methods. In legacy-client mode those hand the call to the ZIA legacy client (`LegacyClient.ZiaClient`), while the ZTW-specific `...Resource` methods hand it to the ZTW legacy client. The affected services are activation, the provisioning URL, workload groups, and the shared `ReadPage` helper that the ZPA-resource lookup uses.

ztw-services-use-generic-legacy-path.conditions: This is the ZTW instance of the routing defect described for ZCC in [[zcc.sdk-go.legacy-routing]]. It holds only when the provider is configured with `use_legacy_client` (or `ZSCALER_USE_LEGACY_CLIENT=true`); the default is OneAPI, where the generic methods run the shared OneAPI path and this does not occur. ztw-update-deref-after-ignored-assertion.statement: `forwarding_rules.Update` ignores the result of its type assertion and then reads the rule's ID. The shared update helper returns a nil result with a nil error for an empty reply body, so if the API answers the PUT with an empty body (for example 204 No Content) the call panics with a nil pointer dereference instead of returning an error.

provider-reaches-ztw-update-deref.statement: The ZTC provider at v0.2.0 calls these update functions from the update paths of its forwarding, DNS, and log rule resources, gateways, groups, services, location template, and provisioning URL resources, and discards the returned value, so it relies on the SDK call not panicking. The provider installs no `recover`, so a panic ends the provider process. The rule resources also call `forwarding_rules.Update` from the reorder helpers.

provider-reaches-ztw-update-deref.conditions: Search: `git -C vendor/terraform-provider-ztc grep -n -E '\.(Update|UpdateAccountGroups)\(ctx' v0.2.0 -- ztc` lists the call sites; `git grep -n 'recover()' v0.2.0` finds none. Whether the panic happens depends on the API answering a PUT with an empty body (gap ztw-update-empty-reply). Effect on the reorder helpers (a goroutine ending before it signals completion) was not traced here; see [[cloud-connector.terraform.rule-order]].

pointer-mutators-deref-before-nil-check.statement: `forwarding_rules.Create` and `Update` take a pointer and dereference it (`*rules`) when building the call to the generic helper. A nil pointer panics at that dereference. The generic helpers' own nil-payload checks cannot catch it, because the value passed to them is already a struct copy that is never a nil interface.

provider-passes-non-nil-pointers.statement: The ZTC provider's create and update paths pass the address of a locally built request (`&req`) or a rule taken from a list, so the provider does not hand these functions a nil pointer.
provider-passes-non-nil-pointers.conditions: Same search as for the update call sites (`git grep -n -E '\.(Update|Create)[A-Za-z]*\(ctx' v0.2.0 -- ztc`); every match reviewed passes `&req`, `&rule`, or a rule variable from the enclosing list loop. The loop variables were not traced to a possible nil, so this is a code-reading result, not a proof.

location-vpc-info-value-structs.statement: The ZTW location request holds `VPCInfo` by value with `omitempty`, and `VPCInfo` holds `CloudMeta` by value with `omitempty`. Every member of both is itself `omitempty`, so a location whose VPC information is unset still has two struct-valued fields that Go's JSON encoder never omits.

upstream.note: Filing 20 (ZTW SDK services) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

location-write-emits-empty-vpc-object.statement: Creating or updating a location with the VPC information left unset therefore sends `"vpcInfo":{"cloudMeta":{}}` rather than omitting the member. The ZTC provider at v0.2.0 does not reach this: its location management resource is commented out and unregistered, and the location data source only reads.

location-template-editable-always-false.statement: The location template request carries `Editable` as a plain bool with no `omitempty`, and the provider's request builder never sets it. Every create and update of a location template therefore sends `"editable":false` (top level and in the nested `template` object), including an update of a template the server reported as editable. Whether the server honors or ignores that field on a PUT is not established.

ztw-update-empty-reply.title: Whether any ZTW update endpoint answers a PUT with an empty body
ztw-update-empty-reply.blocks: saying whether the ignored-assertion dereference in the ZTW update functions panics in practice
ztw-update-empty-reply.detail: Against a scratch tenant, send a valid PUT through each ZTW update function the provider calls (forwarding, DNS, and log rules, gateways, groups, services, location template, provisioning URL) and record the status code and whether the body is empty. Any 204 or empty 200 is a panic path.
